This judgment shall dispose of the present reference forwarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as "LAC") under the provisions of Sections 30-31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter "L.A. Act").

The reference seeks an adjudication from this Court regarding the apportionment of compensation money awarded for land acquired in Village Ghuman Hera, Delhi,
due to a dispute having arisen between the Interested Parties (IPs) herein as to their respective entitlements.

FACTUAL BACKGROUND AND GENESIS OF THE REFERENCE:
2.

The undisputed facts leading to the present reference are that lands situated in the Revenue Estate of Village Ghuman Hera, Delhi, were acquired by the Government for a public purpose,
namely, the "Construction of New 765/400/220 KV Ultra High Voltage Sub Station to Facilitate Mega Power to Delhi Capital Region."
The acquisition was made pursuant to Award No. 03/2011 dated 07.01.2011, passed by the LAC.

3. The communication from the ADM/LAC indicates that a sum of Rs. 2,09,76,403/- (Rupees Two Crore Nine Lakh Seventy- Six Thousand Four Hundred and Three Only), representing the compensation for the acquired land recorded in the name of Sh. A.S. Gaur (since deceased,
represented by IP No. 1/The Claimants), was tendered for deposit in the Court.

This deposit, made vide consolidated cheque number 847127 dated 27.12.2013, was effected in compliance with directions issued by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in CM No. 20788/2013 and CM (M) No.
1412/2013.

4. The ADM/LAC was constrained to make the present reference as Smt. Laxmi Devi (IP No. 2/The Objector) raised objections concerning the rightful entitlement to the compensation amount pertaining to specific Khasra numbers, namely Khasra Nos. 14, 15, 17, and 23/1 in Mustatil No. 43,
situated in Village Ghuman Hera.
As per the revenue records considered by the LAC, Sh. A.S. Gaur was the recorded owner of the subject land for which the aforementioned compensation was assessed.

PARTICULARS OF THE INTERESTED PARTIES AND THEIR RESPECTIVE CLAIMS:

sentences.text: The original IP No. 1, Sh. A.S. Gaur, unfortunately, demised during the pendency of these proceedings (in fact, on 23.07.2008, prior to the passing of the Award).

His legal representatives (LRs), namely his sons Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur, were duly substituted on record by an order of this Court dated 04.04.2025.
6.

The claim articulated by IP No. 1, through the claim petition filed by the LRs and the evidence subsequently adduced, is predicated on the following assertions:
a.

The late Sh. A.S. Gaur was the absolute owner and Bhumidhar in possession of a parcel of land which included, inter alia, Khasra Nos. 12 (3-17), 13 (4-16), 14 (4-16), 15 (1-14), 17 (3- 19), 18 (4-16), 19 (5-03), 23/1 (3-08), and 28 (0-03), falling within Mustatil No. 43 of Village Ghuman Hera, New Delhi.

He was also the owner of a tube-well situated in Khasra No.
14. b.

Out of the aforesaid holdings, land comprising Khasra Nos. 14 (4 Bigha 16 Biswas), 15 (1 Bigha 14 Biswas), 17 (3 Bigha 19 Biswas), and 23/1 (3 Bigha 08 Biswas) (aggregating to 13 Bigha 17 Biswas), along with the tube-well in Khasra No. 14, was acquired under the subject Award.
It is the compensation for this specific acquired land that is the subject matter of the present reference.

c. The proprietary title to this land was acquired by the late Sh.
A.S. Gaur from Smt. Laxmi Devi (IP No. 2/The Objector) herself.

This transaction was effected through her duly appointed General Power of Attorney (GPA) holder, Sh.
Gajender Singh S/o Sh. Parbhu Singh.

The sale was concretized by way of four distinct registered Sale Deeds, all executed on 14.11.1996.
d.

Following these registered sale transactions, the necessary mutation in the revenue records was carried out in favour of the late Sh. A.S. Gaur on 13.01.1997, formally recognizing him as the recorded owner/Bhumidhar.
e.

The present claimants, Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur, derive their exclusive right to claim the compensation by virtue of inheritance from their father, late Sh. A.S. Gaur, and also based on a registered Relinquishment Deed dated 10.10.2008 (Ex. P4).

Vide this deed, their sisters (Mrs.
Bindu Bhardawaj and Mrs. Dimple Gaur, also LRs of late Sh. A.S. Gaur) relinquished their respective shares and interests in the subject property/compensation in favour of their brothers, the claimants herein.
The wife of late Sh. A.S. Gaur, Smt. Sheela Gaur, had also since passed away.

f. Crucially, it is asserted that Smt. Laxmi Devi (IP No. 2) had previously instituted seven distinct civil suits, wherein she had challenged the legality and validity of the GPA and the subsequent sale deeds executed in favour of Sh. A.S. Gaur.

These suits, seeking reliefs such as cancellation of Union Of India vs A S Gaur And Ors on 31 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171426698/
3 documents, declaration of title, and permanent injunction, were all comprehensively dismissed by competent Civil Courts vide orders dated 25.08.2017 and final judgments and decrees dated 10.02.2020.

g. On the strength of these facts and legal outcomes, the LRs of Sh. A.S. Gaur assert an indefeasible and exclusive right to receive the entire compensation amount of Rs. 2,09,76,403/-, currently held in deposit with this Court, to be apportioned equally between Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur.
7. The reference documentation from the ADM/LAC identifies Smt. Laxmi Devi W/o Sh. Pratap Singh as the objector.
Her objection, which triggered this reference, was specifically against the payment of compensation to Sh. A.S. Gaur for the land comprising Khasra Nos. 14, 15, 17, and 23/1 in Mustatil No. 43.
As will be detailed below, Smt. Laxmi Devi did not participate in the proceedings before this Court despite service.

PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THIS COURT:
8. Upon receipt of the reference, notices were issued to the Interested Parties.
An application under Order XXII Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) was filed on behalf of the LRs of the deceased IP No. 1, Sh. A.S. Gaur, for their substitution.
9. The record reflects that notices of the reference petition, as well as the application for substitution, were directed to be served upon Smt. Laxmi Devi (IP No. 2).

As detailed in the order of this Court dated 24.01.2025, initial attempts at service upon Smt. Laxmi Devi were met with reports of her being hospitalized and refusals to receive summons on her behalf.

Consequently, fresh notice was directed, with specific instructions for diligent attempts at service, including affixation at a conspicuous part of her premises in case of non-service or refusal.
10.
The order sheet dated 04.04.2025 (forenoon session) records that Smt. Laxmi Devi was duly served by way of affixation on 31.01.2025, in compliance with the previous directions.
Despite such service, Smt. Laxmi Devi failed to enter an appearance before this Court, either in person or through counsel.
Accordingly, she was proceeded against ex-parte.
Her right to file any reply to the application under Order XXII Rule 4 CPC, or to file a statement of claim in the main reference proceedings, was consequently closed.
11. Subsequently, this Court, vide an order passed on 04.04.2025 (afternoon session), allowed the application under Order XXII Rule 4 CPC.
Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur were substituted as the LRs of the deceased IP No. 1, Sh. A.S. Gaur.

This order took into account the documentary evidence of the demise of Sh. A.S. Gaur and his wife, Smt. Sheela Gaur, and importantly, the registered Relinquishment Deed dated 10.10.2008 (Ex. P4), by which the daughters of Sh. A.S. Gaur had relinquished their shares in favour of the present claimants.

The court also noted the corroborative statements recorded in execution proceedings (M.Ex. No.
229/2022).

EVIDENCE ADDUCED BY THE LRS OF IP NO. 1:
13.
In support of their claim, Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur, one of the LRs of IP No. 1, deposed as IP1W-1.
He tendered his evidence by way of an affidavit, which was exhibited as Ex. IP1W-1/A.
In his testimony, IP1W-1 largely reiterated the averments made in the claim petition.

He provided a detailed account of his late father's ownership of the subject land, the manner of its acquisition from Smt. Laxmi Devi (IP No. 2) through her GPA holder by way of four registered sale deeds, the subsequent mutation in his father's name, the relinquishment of shares by his sisters in favour of himself and his brother, and most critically, the comprehensive dismissal of all seven civil suits previously instituted by Smt. Laxmi Devi challenging these transactions.

14. In fortification of this oral testimony, IP1W-1 placed reliance upon and exhibited the following documentary evidence:
a. Copy of the registered Relinquishment Deed dated 10.10.2008 executed by Mrs.
Bindu Bhardawaj and Mrs. Dimple Gaur in favour of Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh.
Rajeev Gaur (previously exhibited as Ex. P4 during the LR impleadment proceedings;
the proposed exhibit mark Ex. IP1W-1/1 was consequently de-exhibited to avoid duplication).
b. A photocopy of the General Power of Attorney (GPA) dated 19.07.1996, purportedly executed by Smt. Laxmi Devi in favour of Sh. Gajender Singh (document tendered as Mark A).

c. Attested copies of the four registered Sale Deeds, all dated 14.11.1996, executed by Smt. Laxmi Devi through her GPA holder, Sh. Gajender Singh, in favour of the late Sh. A.S. Gaur, pertaining to the subject land (collectively exhibited as Ex. IP1W-1/2 (Colly) (OSR) - Original Seen and Returned).
d.

Certified copies of the orders dated 25.08.2017, passed by the concerned Civil Court, dismissing five of the civil suits filed by Smt. Laxmi Devi (collectively exhibited as Ex. IP1W-1/3 (Colly) (OSR)).
e.

Certified copies of the Judgments and Decrees, both dated 10.02.2020, passed by the concerned Civil Courts, dismissing the remaining two civil suits instituted by Smt. Laxmi Devi (exhibited as Ex.
IP1W-1/4 (OSR) and Ex. IP1W-1/5 (OSR) respectively).
15. IP1W-1 further testified that, to the best of his knowledge and information, no appeals preferred by Smt. Laxmi Devi against the dismissal of her aforementioned seven civil suits were pending adjudication.

He concluded by asserting the unequivocal entitlement of himself and his brother, Sh.
Rajeev Gaur, to the entirety of the compensation amount of Rs. 2,09,76,403/-, currently secured in an FDR held with this Court.

Scope of Adjudication under Sections 30-31 of the L.A. Act and Effect of Ex-Parte Proceedings against IP No. 2:
16.
The jurisdiction of this Court in a reference under Sections 30-31 of the L.A. Act is confined to the determination of the "apportionment of the said compensation among the persons interested."

This necessitates an inquiry into the respective titles and interests of the disputing parties in the acquired land, as the right to receive compensation, which is a monetary substitute for the land,
flows from the title or interest held in that land at the time of acquisition.

17. In the instant case, Smt. Laxmi Devi (IP No. 2), despite being duly served with notice of these proceedings by way of affixation (a recognized mode of service, especially following previous evasions/refusals), opted not to participate.
Her consequent ex-parte status means that the assertions made and the evidence adduced by the LRs of IP No. 1 remain uncontroverted and unchallenged on the record.
However, it is trite law that even in ex- parte proceedings, the party leading evidence must stand on its own legs and establish its claim through cogent and credible evidence.
The absence of contest does not automatically entitle the claiming party to relief; the Court must still satisfy itself as to the tenability of the claim.

ASSESSMENT OF CLAIM OF LRS OF IP NO. 1 - SH. A.S. GAUR:
18.

The claim of IP No. 1 rests on establishing, firstly, the title of the late Sh. A.S. Gaur to the acquired land, and secondly, the exclusive entitlement of the present claimants (Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur) to succeed to his interest in the compensation.
Title of Sh. A.S. Gaur to the Acquired Land:
19.

Following is the assessment:
a.
The Sale Deeds (Ex. IP1W-1/2 Colly): The claimants have placed on record copies of four registered Sale Deeds (Ex. IP1W-1/2 Colly), all dated 14.11.1996.

These documents purport to transfer ownership of the subject Khasra numbers (specifically 14, 15, 17, and 23/1 of Mustatil No. 43) from Smt. Laxmi Devi, acting through her GPA holder Sh. Gajender Singh, to the late Sh. A.S. Gaur for valuable consideration.
Being registered documents, these sale deeds carry a presumption of due execution and authenticity and their contents can be presumed to be genuine unless proven otherwise.

The originals were produced for comparison, as indicated by the endorsement "OSR."
b.

Mutation Records: IP1W-1 deposed that following the execution of the sale deeds,
mutation of the land in the revenue records was carried out in the name of Sh. A.S.
Gaur on 13.01.1997.
While it is well-settled that mutation entries are primarily for fiscal purposes and do not, in themselves, create or extinguish title
, they are certainly relevant pieces of evidence indicating possession and the recognition of a person as the owner by the revenue authorities.

This evidence, therefore, buttresses the claim of Union Of India vs A S Gaur And Ors on 31 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171426698/

c. Conclusive Impact of Dismissal of Civil Suits Filed by IP No. 2 (Ex. IP1W-1/3, Ex. IP1W-1/4, Ex.
IP1W-1/5): This is arguably the most decisive aspect of the evidence.

The LRs of IP No. 1 have placed on record certified copies of orders and judgments/decrees demonstrating the dismissal of seven civil suits instituted by Smt. Laxmi Devi (IP No. 2) against her GPA holder Sh. Gajender Singh and the late Sh. A.S. Gaur (predecessor-in-interest of the claimants).

These suits, bearing Nos. CS No.
8614/16, CS No. 12640/16, CS No. 12643/16, CS No. 12644/16, CS No. 12645/16, CS No.
609098/16, and CS No. 612639/16, sought reliefs such as cancellation of the GPA and sale deeds,
declaration of title in her favour, and permanent injunction.
The dismissal of these suits by competent civil courts is of profound legal significance.
These judgments operate with finality on the issues raised therein between the parties (or their privies).

While the precise grounds for dismissal of each suit are detailed in the respective judgments (Ex. IP1W-1/3 to Ex. IP1W-1/5), the overarching effect is that Smt. Laxmi Devi's challenges to the validity of the GPA executed by her and the subsequent sale deeds transacted by her attorney in favour of Sh. A.S. Gaur were judicially considered and rejected.

The principles analogous to res judicata, as embodied in Section 11 of the CPC, would suggest that IP No. 2 cannot be permitted to re-agitate the same issues of title and validity of sale transactions in these collateral proceedings for apportionment of compensation,
having failed to substantiate her claims in direct challenges before the civil courts.

The findings in those suits, which upheld the transactions leading to Sh. A.S. Gaur's title, effectively extinguish any claim Smt. Laxmi Devi might have had to the land, and consequently, to the compensation which is its monetary equivalent.

She had the fullest opportunity to establish her claims of alleged fraud,
misrepresentation, or lack of authority concerning the GPA and sale deeds in those seven suits, and she failed.
The deposition that no appeals are pending against these dismissals further underscores their finality.

Entitlement of the Claimants (Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur):
20.

Following is the analysis:
Devolution of Interest and the Relinquishment Deed (Ex. P4):
Having established the title of the late Sh. A.S. Gaur, the next step is to ascertain the entitlement of the present claimants, Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur, to succeed to his interest.
Sh. A.S. Gaur passed away on 23.07.2008.
His wife, Smt. Sheela Gaur, also subsequently demised.
He was survived by two sons (the claimants) and two daughters (Mrs. Bindu Bhardawaj and Mrs. Dimple Gaur).
The claimants have filed and proved the registered Relinquishment Deed dated 10.10.2008 (Ex. P4).

By this deed, the two daughters of Sh.
A.S. Gaur

expressly relinquished their entire share and interest in the estate of their late father,
including the subject land/compensation, in favour of their brothers, Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur, in equal shares.
A registered relinquishment deed is a valid mode of transferring interest among co-heirs.
This document, coupled with the laws of succession, clearly establishes that the present claimants are the sole persons entitled to the interest of the late Sh. A.S. Gaur.

Nexus between Title to Land and Right to Compensation:
21.

It is a fundamental principle in land acquisition law that compensation is payable to the person(s) who had an interest in the land at the time the notification under Section 4 of the L.A. Act was issued, and whose interest has been acquired.
Compensation is, in essence, the monetary value of the proprietary or other interests extinguished by the acquisition.
Therefore, the right to receive compensation directly flows from, and is correlative to, the title or interest held in the acquired land.

Having established that Sh. A.S. Gaur was the rightful owner of the acquired Khasra Nos. 14,
15, 17, and 23/1 in Mustatil No. 43 at the relevant time, his LRs (the claimants herein,
by virtue of inheritance and relinquishment) are consequently entitled to the compensation awarded for this specific land.

Conclusion on Entitlement to Compensation for the Disputed Khasras:
22.

The entire conspectus of the unrebutted oral and documentary evidence leads to the irresistible conclusion that the late Sh. A.S. Gaur was the true and lawful owner of the acquired land comprising Khasra Nos. 14 (4-16), 15 (1-14), 17 (3-19), and 23/1 (3- 08) in Mustatil No. 43, Village Ghuman Hera, along with the tube- well thereon.

The objections raised by Smt. Laxmi Devi (IP No. 2), which formed the very basis for this reference, have been demonstrated to be entirely devoid of merit, particularly in light of the definitive dismissal of her seven civil suits wherein she had agitated her claims concerning these very properties and transactions.
23. The compensation amount of Rs. 2,09,76,403/- was deposited in court specifically for the land recorded in the name of Sh. A.S. Gaur under Award No. 03/2011.
The evidence confirms that this compensation pertains to the land to which the claimants have successfully established their predecessor's title and their own derivative rights.

There is no other claimant before this Court staking a claim to this amount, and the claim of IP No. 2 has been effectively negated by her own failed litigations and her subsequent ex-parte status in these proceedings.

FINAL DECISION AND OPERATIVE PART:
24.

For the foregoing detailed reasons, this Court finds that the LRs of IP No. 1, namely Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur, have successfully established their exclusive entitlement to the compensation amount in dispute.
The objections that led to this reference are found to be untenable.

25. Accordingly, it is hereby held and declared that Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur S/o Late Sh. A.S. Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur S/o Late Sh. A.S. Gaur are jointly entitled to receive the entire compensation Union Of India vs A S Gaur And Ors on 31 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171426698/
8 amount, together with all accrued interest thereon, if any, which is presently lying in deposit with this Court in connection with Award No. 03/2011 for Village Ghuman Hera, pertaining to Khasra Nos. 43//14 (4-16), 43//15 (1-14), 43//17 (3-19), and 43//23/1 (3-08) along with a tube-well in Khasra No. 43//14.

26. Consequently, the present reference under Sections 30- 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, is answered by holding that the entire compensation amount stated above shall be apportioned and paid to Sh. Sanjay Kumar Gaur and Sh. Rajeev Gaur in equal moiety.
27. A copy of this Order be dispatched forthwith to the office of the Land Acquisition Collector (South-West), Delhi, for their information and necessary action at their end.
28. After full compliance with the above direction, the file of this reference shall be consigned to the Record Room.

It is a fundamental principle in land acquisition law that compensation is payable to the person(s) who had an interest in the land at the time the notification under Section 4 of the L.A. Act was issued, and whose interest has been acquired.
Compensation is, in essence, the monetary value of the proprietary or other interests extinguished by the acquisition.
Therefore, the right to receive compensation directly flows from, and is correlative to, the title or interest held in the acquired land.
Having established that Sh. A.S. Gaur was the rightful owner of the acquired Khasra Nos. 14,
15, 17, and 23/1 in Mustatil No. 43 at the relevant time, his LRs (the claimants herein,
by virtue of inheritance and relinquishment) are consequently entitled to the compensation awarded for this specific land.
